exercises.questionText: Use the graph of $y=\cos(x)$ for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$ (a cosine curve starting at $(0^\circ,1)$, reaching $-1$ at $180^\circ$ and returning to $1$ at $360^\circ$) to determine approximate answers to the equation for the domain $0\le x\le360^\circ$. Check your answers using a calculator. $\cos(x)=0.9$

solution.formula: Solutions of $\cos(x)=k$ are where the horizontal line $y=k$ meets the curve; by symmetry, if $x_1$ is one solution in $[0^\circ,180^\circ]$ the other is $360^\circ-x_1$.
steps: Draw the line $y=0.9$ across the graph; it cuts the curve twice, symmetrically about $x=180^\circ$. Both intersections are near the ends of the domain, where the graph is high.
solution.tip: The cosine graph is symmetric about $x=180^\circ$, so the two solutions add to $360^\circ$.

exercises.questionText: Sam measured the depth of water at the end of the Intergate jetty at various times on Thursday 13 August 2020. Her results were: 6 am 1.5 m, 7 am 1.8 m, 8 am 2.3 m, 9 am 2.6 m, 10 am 2.5 m, 11 am 2.2 m, 12 pm 1.8 m, 1 pm 1.2 m, 2 pm 0.8 m, 3 pm 0.5 m, 4 pm 0.6 m, 5 pm 1.0 m, 6 pm 1.3 m, 7 pm 1.8 m, 8 pm 2.2 m, 9 pm 2.5 m. a. Plot the data.

solution.formula: Sinusoidal model: amplitude $=\frac{\max-\min}{2}$, mean level $=\frac{\max+\min}{2}$, period = time for one complete cycle (e.g. twice the time from a maximum to the next minimum).
steps: Given: 16 readings from 6 am to 9 pm. Goal: a plot of depth against time.
Horizontal axis: time from 5 am to 9 pm (1 unit per hour); vertical axis: depth from 0 to 3.0 m.
Join with a smooth curve: the depth rises to a high of about 2.6 m at 9 am, falls to a low of about 0.5 m at 3 pm, then rises again towards 9 pm.
solution.finalAnswer: The plot is a smooth wave-like curve: a high of 2.6 m at 9 am, a low of 0.5 m at 3 pm, and rising again to 2.5 m by 9 pm.
solution.tip: Join tide data with a smooth curve rather than straight segments; tides follow a sine-type pattern.

exercises.questionText: Sam measured the depth of water at the end of the Intergate jetty at various times on Thursday 13 August 2020. Her results were: 6 am 1.5 m, 7 am 1.8 m, 8 am 2.3 m, 9 am 2.6 m, 10 am 2.5 m, 11 am 2.2 m, 12 pm 1.8 m, 1 pm 1.2 m, 2 pm 0.8 m, 3 pm 0.5 m, 4 pm 0.6 m, 5 pm 1.0 m, 6 pm 1.3 m, 7 pm 1.8 m, 8 pm 2.2 m, 9 pm 2.5 m. b. Determine: i. the period, ii. the amplitude.

solution.formula: Sinusoidal model: amplitude $=\frac{\max-\min}{2}$, mean level $=\frac{\max+\min}{2}$, period = time for one complete cycle (e.g. twice the time from a maximum to the next minimum).
steps: Given: high 2.6 m at 9 am, low 0.5 m at 3 pm. Goal: period and amplitude.
High to low takes about $6$ to $6\frac14$ hours (the next high is due a little after 9 pm, as the depth is still rising at 9 pm).
i. One full cycle is high → low → high, about $2\times6\frac14=12\frac12$ hours. (This matches the known tidal period of about 12 h 25 min.)
solution.finalAnswer: i. The period is about $12\frac12$ hours. ii. The amplitude is 1.05 m.
solution.tip: Amplitude is half the difference between the highest and lowest values, not the highest value itself.

exercises.questionText: Sam measured the depth of water at the end of the Intergate jetty at various times on Thursday 13 August 2020. Her results were: 6 am 1.5 m, 7 am 1.8 m, 8 am 2.3 m, 9 am 2.6 m, 10 am 2.5 m, 11 am 2.2 m, 12 pm 1.8 m, 1 pm 1.2 m, 2 pm 0.8 m, 3 pm 0.5 m, 4 pm 0.6 m, 5 pm 1.0 m, 6 pm 1.3 m, 7 pm 1.8 m, 8 pm 2.2 m, 9 pm 2.5 m. c. Sam fishes from the jetty when the depth is a maximum. Specify these times for the next 3 days.

solution.formula: Successive maximums are one period ($12\frac12$ h) apart.
steps: Given: a maximum at 9:00 am Thursday, period $12\frac12$ hours. Goal: maximum times on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
Thursday: 9:00 am, then $9{:}00\text{ am}+12\text{ h }30\text{ min}=9{:}30$ pm.
Friday: $9{:}30\text{ pm}+12\text{ h }30\text{ min}=10{:}00$ am; then 10:30 pm.
Sunday: 12:00 noon; the next one is 12:30 am Monday.
solution.finalAnswer: Maximum depths (fishing times): Friday 10:00 am and 10:30 pm; Saturday 11:00 am and 11:30 pm; Sunday 12:00 noon.
solution.tip: Each day the high tides are about 1 hour later than the day before (two periods = 25 hours).

exercises.questionText: Sam measured the depth of water at the end of the Intergate jetty at various times on Thursday 13 August 2020. Her results were: 6 am 1.5 m, 7 am 1.8 m, 8 am 2.3 m, 9 am 2.6 m, 10 am 2.5 m, 11 am 2.2 m, 12 pm 1.8 m, 1 pm 1.2 m, 2 pm 0.8 m, 3 pm 0.5 m, 4 pm 0.6 m, 5 pm 1.0 m, 6 pm 1.3 m, 7 pm 1.8 m, 8 pm 2.2 m, 9 pm 2.5 m. d. Sam’s mother can moor her yacht when the depth is above 1.5 m. Determine during what periods she can moor the yacht on Sunday 16 January (as printed; Sunday three days after the Thursday is 16 August).

solution.formula: Model: $D=1.55+1.05\cos\left(\frac{360^\circ}{12.5}(t-t_{\max})\right)$, where $t$ is in hours and $t_{\max}$ is the time of a high tide.
steps: Given: mean level $=\frac{2.6+0.5}{2}=1.55$ m, amplitude 1.05 m, period 12.5 h, Sunday high tides at 11:30 pm Saturday, 12:00 noon Sunday and 12:30 am Monday (from part c). Goal: when $D>1.5$ on Sunday.
Convert to time: $\frac{92.73^\circ}{360^\circ}\times12.5\text{ h}\approx3.22$ h $\approx3$ h 13 min either side of each high tide.
High at 11:30 pm Saturday: depth above 1.5 m until $11{:}30\text{ pm}+3\text{ h }13\text{ min}=2{:}43$ am Sunday.
High at 12:30 am Monday: from $12{:}30\text{ am}-3\text{ h }13\text{ min}=9{:}17$ pm Sunday.
solution.finalAnswer: Using the sinusoidal model, she can moor the yacht on Sunday from midnight until about 2:43 am, from about 8:47 am to 3:13 pm, and after about 9:17 pm. (The book gives: until 1:45 am, 8 am to 2:15 pm, and after 8:30 pm; answers read from a hand-drawn graph will vary.)
solution.tip: Because 1.5 m is just below the mean level of 1.55 m, the yacht can be moored for slightly more than half of each cycle.

exercises.questionText: Solve $\sqrt3\sin(x^\circ)=\cos(x^\circ)$ for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$.

solution.formula: $\tan(x)=\frac{\sin(x)}{\cos(x)}$; CAST rule: in $[0^\circ,360^\circ]$, sine is positive in quadrants 1 and 2, cosine in quadrants 1 and 4, tangent in quadrants 1 and 3. Quadrant angles from a reference angle $\theta$: $\theta$, $180^\circ-\theta$, $180^\circ+\theta$, $360^\circ-\theta$.
steps: If $\cos(x)=0$ then $\sin(x)=\pm1$ and the equation would read $\pm\sqrt3=0$, which is false; so $\cos(x)\neq0$ and we may divide by it.
Reference angle $30^\circ$; tangent positive in quadrants 1 and 3.
solution.tip: Dividing by $\cos(x)$ turns a sin–cos equation into a tan equation; check that $\cos(x)=0$ is not a solution first.

exercises.questionText: Solve $2\sin(x^\circ)+\cos(x^\circ)=0$ for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$.

solution.formula: $\tan(x)=\frac{\sin(x)}{\cos(x)}$; CAST rule: in $[0^\circ,360^\circ]$, sine is positive in quadrants 1 and 2, cosine in quadrants 1 and 4, tangent in quadrants 1 and 3. Quadrant angles from a reference angle $\theta$: $\theta$, $180^\circ-\theta$, $180^\circ+\theta$, $360^\circ-\theta$.
steps: Given: $2\sin(x)+\cos(x)=0$. Goal: all $x$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ]$, to 2 decimal places.
Rearrange: $2\sin(x)=-\cos(x)$. ($\cos(x)=0$ is not a solution, since then $2\sin(x)=\pm2\neq0$.)
Reference angle: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)\approx26.57^\circ$; tangent negative in quadrants 2 and 4.
solution.tip: Use the positive value $\frac12$ to find the reference angle, then place it in the quadrants where tan is negative.

exercises.questionText: Solve $2\sin^2(x^\circ)+3\sin(x^\circ)-2=0$ for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$.

solution.formula: Treat as a quadratic in $\sin(x)$: let $a=\sin(x)$, so $2a^2+3a-2=0$. Also $-1\le\sin(x)\le1$.
steps: $\sin(x)=\frac12$: reference angle $30^\circ$, sine positive in quadrants 1 and 2, so $x=30^\circ$ or $x=150^\circ$.
solution.tip: Always reject values of $\sin(x)$ or $\cos(x)$ outside $[-1,1]$.

exercises.questionText: The grad ($^g$) is another measurement used when measuring the size of angles. A grad is equivalent to $\frac{1}{400}$ of a full circle. Write the following as grads (1 grad is written as $1^g$): $90^\circ$

solution.formula: Full circle $=360^\circ=400^g$, so $1^\circ=\frac{400}{360}=\frac{10}{9}$ grads.
steps: Given: $90^\circ$. Goal: the angle in grads.
solution.tip: A right angle is $100^g$, so each quarter turn adds $100^g$.
